overall: As of 07:45 ET (04:45 local PT), Los Angeles is in pre-dawn hours with a current temperature of 68°F and a running max of 70°F set around 03:52 ET — entirely consistent with overnight cooling. Temperature has been flat-to-slightly-cooling since that overnight peak, which is normal at this hour. There is no meaningful intraday warming signal yet, but the bulk of the heating window (roughly 07:00–16:00 local) still lies ahead.
forecast_obs_notes: Model agreement is poor: GFS (84.0°F) and ECMWF (83.8°F) cluster at the hot end, HRRR (81.4°F) aligns closely with the NWS official forecast of ~81°F, and NBM is a notable outlier at 75.8°F, pulling the probabilistic D1_NOW distribution cooler than the deterministic guidance warrants. The NWS Heat Advisory covers the Central Valley (102–107°F), not coastal LA, confirming a strong inland heat event is underway but that marine influence will moderate downtown/urban LA temperatures considerably.
max_temp_prediction: The weight of evidence — NWS official 81°F, HRRR 81.4°F, and the broader GFS/ECMWF 83–84°F warm envelope — points to a daily high in the 80–82°F range. The active even-bucket market's top bucket of 74–75°F (43.2% D1_NOW) appears to be pulled low by NBM and the current cool morning readings, but it meaningfully underestimates the likely outcome relative to NWS and NWP guidance; the 80–81F even bucket at 21.4% looks undervalued. Best estimate is ~81°F with moderate-to-good confidence, with upside risk toward 83–84°F if offshore flow strengthens as GFS/ECMWF suggest.
